title: Meta earnings: Stock drops 5% as EPS misses Wall Street estimates
byline: Charles Rollet, Pranav Dixit, Henry Chandonnet, Steven Tweedie, Max Adams, Hugh Langley, Samuel O'Brient
excerpt: Meta reported its Q2 earnings report, with earnings per share lighter than expected. Its analyst call kicks off at 4:30 p.m. ET.
content_html:
Read in app

Meta's stock slumped in after hours trading on Wednesday after the tech giant delivered earnings per share below Wall Street's estimates.

Meta is one of the "hyperscalers" spending huge sums on its AI projects, from data centers to its own large language models, and investors are getting impatient to see what those efforts have yielded.

The company's advertising revenue — its cash cow — rose 27% to $59.36 billion, beating analysts' $59.07 billion estimate. Ad impressions grew 14%, while the average price per ad climbed 12%.

"AI is accelerating our core business today, powering our next generation of products, and opening the door to entirely new enterprise opportunities," Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in an earnings release. "The results are already showing, and I'm optimistic about the potential ahead."

Ahead of Meta's call with analysts at 4:30 p.m., all eyes will be on Meta's capex, the all important figure that's come to dominate investors' reactions to earnings lately. Alphabet and Tesla set the tone last week with their heightened spending outlooks, causing both stocks to tumble after results.

Meta's stock is down 10% year to date.

Copied!

Meta's smart glasses are still a small part of its business

Reality Labs — the division that oversees Meta's hardware efforts — made $431 million in quarterly revenue, up 16% year over year. While that's solid growth, the division remains tiny, generating less than 1% of the cash generated by Meta's ad business.

Copied!

Meta's Q3 revenue guidance

Wall Street expects Meta to deliver $63.17 billion in revenue for the third qurater. That's on the high end of the guidance CFO Susan Li gives: $61-64 billion.

Copied!

Capex guidance narrows, but remains on track

As AI spending balloons, investors and analysts alike are keeping an eye on Meta's future spending plans. CFO Susan Li says Meta expects capital expenditures to be between $130-145 billion for the year, narrowed slightly from its prior outlook. Wall Street expected about $135.79 billion, keeping it squarely within the guidance.

Copied!

Meta's lofty legal and severance costs

The company reports $42.03 billion in costs and expenses for the quarter — including some additional charges that upped the bill. Meta paid $2.4 billion in charges related to its "legal proceedings" and $1.18 billion in severance expenses after it laid off roughly 10% of its workforce in May.

Copied!

Meta's Q2 earnings are here — see the key numbers

  • Revenue: $60.8 billion vs. $60.23 billion estimate
  • EPS: $6.18 vs. $7.14 estimate
  • Advertising revenue: $59.36 billion vs. $59.07 billion estimate
  • Reality Labs revenue: $431 million vs. $428.7 million estimate
  • Capex: $31.08 billion

Copied!

Analyst: Meta is "trading people for compute"

Meta's AI push isn't just transforming its products. It is remaking the company itself, Forrester VP and research director Mike Proulx told Business Insider.

"Meta's AI bet is as much cultural as it is technological," Proulx said. "The company is trading people for compute and replacing organizational depth with infrastructure at a moment when execution is the mandate."

Meta shares were down about 1% heading toward the closing bell.

Meta's $145 billion AI bet is still a "trust Zuckerberg" story

Meta plans to spend between $125 billion and $145 billion on capital expenditures this year, much of it on data centers and computing infrastructure to power its AI ambitions.

But unlike Alphabet and Microsoft, it doesn't currently have an established cloud business generating revenue from all that infrastructure, Motley Fool contributing tech analyst Anders Bylund told Business Insider.

But unlike Alphabet and Microsoft, it doesn't currently have an established cloud business generating revenue from all that infrastructure, Motley Fool contributing tech analyst Anders Bylund told Business Insider.

"The hyperscalers can point to direct revenue," Bylund said. "Meta has to point to Zuckerberg's long-term AI conviction."
That could change. Meta is reportedly developing a cloud business that could sell outside customers access to AI models and excess computing power.

For now, investors are being asked to take another expensive bet on Zuckerberg's vision. Investors have heard this pitch before: Zuckerberg's metaverse bet has racked up more than $50 billion in losses so far.

Copied!

Is the "trust toll" a problem for Meta?

A key question on investors' minds is whether Meta's AI spending is boosting its all-important digital advertising business. However, Meta may be facing a "trust toll" thanks to its AI-generated advertising tools, said Forrester analyst Mike Proulx.

Business Insider reported earlier this month that its AI ad tools have been causing chaos for some brands. "That's a big problem for a company that depends on ad revenue," Proulx said.

Copied!

Compute is king

The tech industry's rush for compute isn't slowing down, and Bloomberg recently reported that Meta is developing plans to build its own cloud infrastructure that it could lease to customers.

As Google, Amazon, and Microsoft can attest, it's a good business to be in right now, and one that would help Meta justify its deep investments elsewhere. It's possible we'll hear more about these plans on Meta's earnings call.

Copied!

Is Meta doing too much?

Investors love a clean strategy — but right now, Meta is spinning a lot of plates. "Meta spent the quarter cutting jobs, reorganizing around AI, launching new products, testing new apps, expanding subscriptions, pushing further into smart glasses, and pouring billions more into AI infrastructure," said Forrester analyst Mike Proulx.

"Investors should spend less time counting Meta's AI announcements and more time evaluating whether the company can handle this much disruption at once," he added.

Copied!

Needham says wait until capex cycle is over to buy the stock

Needham is less bullish, maintaining a Hold rating and a more muted $606 price target, about 2% higher than current levels. Analyst Laura Martin says that her team favors waiting to purchase Meta stock until the current capex cycle is over, citing concerns about its plans for growth.

"We retain our HOLD, because we believe that META's strategy diffusion destroys economic value," she wrote. "We think META is asking for too much capital for too many projects, and since competition is intense, strategy dilution lowers the odds that it will succeed at any of them." It cited projects like its Ray-Ban glasses, the Metaverse, and Reality Labs as having uncertain futures in terms of profitability.

Copied!

RBC says 'path to commercialization' needed to validate capex

RBC sees Meta as the tech stock with the biggest opportunity for investor sentiment to improve. Analyst Brad Erickson maintains an Outperform rating and a $810 price target.

Erickson added that if management increases 2026 capex to the forecasted $215 billion, it would likely help position Meta as a competitive force in cloud infrastructure.

在应用程序中阅读

科技巨头 Meta 的每股收益低于华尔街预期，周三盘后交易中该股暴跌。

Meta 是“超大规模企业”之一，在人工智能项目上投入了大量资金，从数据中心到自己的大型语言模型，投资者都迫不及待地想看看这些努力取得了什么成果。

该公司的广告收入（其摇钱树）增长了 27%，达到 593.6 亿美元，超出了分析师预期的 590.7 亿美元。 广告展示次数增长了 14%，而每个广告的平均价格上涨了 12%。

Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格在财报中表示：“人工智能正在加速我们今天的核心业务，为我们的下一代产品提供动力，并为全新的企业机会打开大门。” “结果已经显现，我对未来的潜力感到乐观。”

在下午 4:30 Meta 与分析师举行电话会议之前，所有人的目光都将集中在 Meta 的资本支出上，这是最近主导投资者对收益反应的最重要的数字。 Alphabet 和特斯拉上周以更高的支出前景定下了基调，导致两家公司的股价在公布财报后均暴跌。

Meta 的股价今年迄今已下跌 10%。

“超大规模企业可以带来直接收入，”比伦德说。 “Meta 必须指出扎克伯格对人工智能的长期信念。”这可能会改变。 据报道，Meta 正在开发一项云业务，可以向外部客户出售人工智能模型和多余计算能力。

目前，投资者被要求对扎克伯格的愿景进行另一次昂贵的押注。 投资者以前听过这样的说法：扎克伯格的元宇宙赌注迄今为止已累计损失超过 500 亿美元。

“信任费”对 Meta 来说是个问题吗？

投资者心中的一个关键问题是 Meta 的人工智能支出是否正在提振其最重要的数字广告业务。 然而，Forrester 分析师迈克·普鲁克斯 (Mike Proulx) 表示，由于其人工智能生成的广告工具，Meta 可能面临“信任损失”。

《商业内幕》本月早些时候报道称，其人工智能广告工具给一些品牌造成了混乱。 “对于一家依赖广告收入的公司来说，这是一个大问题，”普鲁克斯说。

计算为王

科技行业对计算的热潮并未放缓，彭博社最近报道称，Meta 正在制定计划，建立自己的云基础设施，并将其租赁给客户。

正如谷歌、亚马逊和微软可以证明的那样，这是一项目前值得涉足的好业务，并且将有助于 Meta 证明其在其他地方的深度投资是合理的。 我们可能会在 Meta 的财报电话会议上听到更多有关这些计划的信息。

Meta 做得太多了吗？

投资者喜欢干净的策略——但现在，Meta 正在做很多事情。 Forrester 分析师迈克·普鲁克斯 (Mike Proulx) 表示：“Meta 在本季度裁员、围绕人工智能进行重组、推出新产品、测试新应用、扩大订阅量、进一步推进智能眼镜业务，并向人工智能基础设施投入数十亿美元。”

他补充道：“投资者应该花更少的时间来计算 Meta 的人工智能公告，而应该花更多的时间来评估该公司是否能够立即应对如此大的干扰。”

Needham表示等到资本支出周期结束后再购买股票

Needham 的乐观情绪有所减弱，维持持有评级，目标价为 606 美元，比当前水平高出约 2%。 分析师劳拉·马丁 (Laura Martin) 表示，她的团队倾向于等到当前资本支出周期结束后再购买 Meta 股票，理由是对其增长计划感到担忧。

“我们保留持有评级，因为我们认为 META 的战略扩散破坏了经济价值，”她写道。 “我们认为 META 为太多项目需要太多资金，而且由于竞争激烈，战略稀释降低了它在任何项目上取得成功的几率。” 该公司表示，雷朋眼镜、Metaverse 和 Reality Labs 等项目的盈利前景存在不确定性。
